reply.note:
Setup and cleanup blocks ran verbatim and succeeded (cleanup left change.patch and inputs.json in /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/build/review-1-opus). I reviewed the whole change 1bebd14..d004f80 against the frozen PRD and spec views, and found no defect the implementation rubric allows me to report.

What I checked in the code:
- src/login.js handler order follows DEC-003 and DEC-010: validation, then the arrival check(), then gate.run(). Inside the gate task, begin() runs before users.has, verifyAsync or the dummy hashPasswordAsync.
- A 503 changes no limiter state.
- end() runs on both the success and the reject path, and a rejected verification answers 500 without counting as a failure.
- The gate releases its slot in finally before the response, and queued tasks start in FIFO order.
- Retry-After is ceil((oldest + 60000 - now) / 1000) when 5 timestamps remain, and 1 when the lock is due to in-flight attempts.
- The session store and the limiter are each capped at 10000: expired, idle records are pruned first, then the oldest record is evicted.
- The body cap is 4096 bytes and returns 413 with connection: close; validation is 1..64 characters for username and 1..1024 for password, otherwise 400.
- The bodies are the fixed DEC-005 ones, and the 503 body is the 401 body.
- The dummy hash is read from the users module object at call time, as DEC-004 requires.
- src/users.js only adds hashPasswordAsync and verifyAsync; the existing exports are unchanged.
- src/server.js keeps GET /health, the 404 fallback and the existing options.
- A grep for console or process.stdout/stderr in src/*.js finds only the existing 'listening on' line.

The new tests cover every acceptance criterion I looked at.

Observed: npm test in the review worktree reported 32 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail. I did not run any proof command from the canonical feature file.

Two things I looked at and decided not to report:
- When the limiter is full, it can evict a record that still has an attempt in verification. This is within accepted risk RISK-002.
- Once the limiter holds 10000 live records, pruning in track() scans all of them for each new username. That is bounded by the gate and costs far less than one scrypt call.
